South Australia.

preserved via rapid precipitation from a silica-rich ocean than Tarhan et al. hypothesized

p:
In 2005, Swedish researchers studying flawed choice recall devised an experiment in
which participants were shown two photos of different faces and asked to select the one
they found more attractive. The researchers appeared to give the participants the photo
they had chosen, but in fact used sleight of hand to give them the photo of the person
they had not chosen. Most participants accepted the swap and, when asked to explain
their initial preference, gave justifications for having chosen the face in the photo they
were given. Subsequent researchers have replicated this finding with other choices,
including jam preferences.
q:
Based on the text, why was the sleight-of-hand step an important part of the
experiment?
o:
It allowed the researchers to control for the possibility that some participants found
the two faces roughly equally attractive.

It enabled the researchers to determine whether the thought processes involved in
selecting which photo had the more attractive face was similar to the thought
processes involved in selecting a preferred jam.

It helped the researchers test whether participants would embrace an outcome they
thought was consistent with their own choices even when it was truly contradictory.

It allowed the researchers to measure the willingness of participants to change their
positions when presented with persuasive counterarguments.
e:
Choice C ("It helped the researchers test whether participants would embrace an outcome they
thought was consistent with their own choices even when it was truly contradictory.") is the correct answer. It best satisfies the prompt requirements based on the textual evidence.

p:

Isaac Asimov, author of Nemesis and The End of Eternity, is highly regarded despite his
mediocre writing style. His prose is workmanlike; his characters are flat and discuss
ideas rather than emotions. That his work is enjoyable despite this is a testament to his
prodigious imagination—even if people read his books only for the ideas, they will have
plenty to consider.
Text 2
Asimov is critiqued for his style, but it is wrong to fault a writer for failing to do what he
never intended to do. For example, although most of his novel Foundation consists of
people discussing science and politics and we find out little about his characters' lives,
Asimov wanted to convey the vast sweep of human history over centuries, and one of
his points is that at such a timescale, individuals don't matter. Thus his lack of
characterization is central to Asimov's thematic aims.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the
evaluation of Asimov's writing style in the underlined claim in Text 1?

By arguing that Asimov's writing style should be judged against the styles of
historians rather than those of fiction writers

By pointing out that the flatness of Asimov's characters is a feature of Nemesis and
The End of Eternity but not of Foundation

By agreeing that Asimov's prose is flawed but disagreeing about the quality of his
characters

By asserting that Asimov's minimal characterization is likely a conscious choice that
helps him convey an important idea

Choice D ("By asserting that Asimov's minimal characterization is likely a conscious choice that

p:
The following text is adapted from Lady Gregory's 1904 play Spreading the News. Jack
Smith and Bartley Fallon have encountered each other at the local fair.
JACK: It isn't to the fair I came myself, but up to the Five Acre Meadow I'm going,
where I have a contract for the hay. We'll get a share of it into tramps [drying stacks] to-
day.
BARTLEY: You will not get it into tramps to-day. The rain will be down on it by evening,
and on myself too. It's seldom I ever started on a journey but the rain would come down
on me before I'd find any place of shelter.
JACK: If it didn't itself, Bartley, it is my belief you would carry a leaky pail on your head
in place of a hat, that way you'd not be without some cause of complaining.
q: Based on the text, what does Jack most likely believe about Bartley?

Bartley will find fault with any situation.
Bartley is a poor judge of the weather.
Bartley is concerned that Jack hasn't prepared for the weather.

p: In 1967, archaeologist James Mellaart claimed that at its peak, Çatalhöyük—a 33-acre Neolithic village in present-day Turkey that dates from approximately 7100 to 5950 BCE —housed between 8,000 to 10,000 residents, an estimate based on the excavation of dense clusters of mud brick buildings that were thought to have been dwellings. Arguing that such estimates should be reevaluated, Ian Kuijt and Arkadiusz Marciniak (2024) cite radiocarbon data and ethnographic modeling that suggest the heterogeneity of building use in Çatalhöyük, with many individual buildings being inhabited for relatively brief periods—20 to 30 years or less—before being abandoned or repurposed for nonresidential functions (e.g., storage). Accordingly, these recent findings challenge the assumption that .
q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
o:
the buildings excavated at Çatalhöyük at the time of Mellaart's research had served
a residential purpose as early as 7100 BCE.

the density of excavated buildings at Çatalhöyük can serve as a proxy for how many
people inhabited the village at a given time.

the use of mud bricks is a reliable indicator that a structure had been used either as
a dwelling or for nonresidential purposes.

the number of buildings at Çatalhöyük would have been sufficient to accommodate a
population that expanded from 8,000 to 10,000 inhabitants by 5950 BCE.
e:
Choice B ("the density of excavated buildings at Çatalhöyük can serve as a proxy for how many
people inhabited the village at a given time.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

p: Chondrite meteorites recovered on Earth tend to show negligible concentrations of sodium-rich evaporites. sodium-rich evaporites are scarce on recovered chondrites in part due to the length

those typically found on Earth.

the sodium evaporite concentrations on Bennu may have once been similar to those

the discrepancy between sodium evaporite concentrations on recovered chondrites

p: Humans are overwhelmingly right-hand dominant (85—90%) and can thus be said to exhibit strong population-level right-handedness (PLRH). Among studies of nonhuman primates, William C. McGrew's 1988 study of captive gorillas purported to show PLRH, while William C. McGrew and colleagues' 1999 study of wild chimpanzees did not. Overall, the studies claiming PLRH in nonhuman primates find much lower incidences of right-handedness than humans exhibit, but it's worth noting that studies of captive primates tend to show significantly greater incidences of right-handedness than studies of wild primates do, therefore raising the possibility that .
q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
o:
the apparent discrepancy between the studies' results may be partly attributable to
the 1988 study using different criteria when assessing hand dominance than were
used in the 1999 study.

the greater exposure to humans among the captive gorillas induced them to acquire
more right-handed behaviors.

the number of individuals in the study of wild chimpanzees is insufficient to preclude
the claim that nonhuman primates exhibit PLRH.

the number of individuals in the study of captive gorillas is insufficient for a robust
claim regarding evidence of PLRH.
e:
Choice B ("the greater exposure to humans among the captive gorillas induced them to acquire
more right-handed behaviors.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

p: Louis-Ferdinand Céline's 1932 novel Journey to the End of the Night is regularly described as autobiographical. That characterization is apt—there are many parallels between the experiences of the novel's protagonist, Ferdinand Bardamu, and those of Céline—but it should not be taken to mean that every person or event depicted in Journey to the End of the Night has a real-life analogue. Much of the novel is pure invention, and readers who neglect this fact and instead focus excessively on correspondences between the novel and Céline's life can thus .

fail to appreciate how much creativity Céline shows in the book.

refuse to acknowledge that Céline drew on real-world material when writing Journey
to the End of the Night.

misrepresent Journey to the End of the Night as being more widely read than it
actually is.
e: Choice B ("fail to appreciate how much creativity Céline shows in the book.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

q:

Independence (published in 1776) was a document that specifically resulted from the
presumably exceptional nature of the soon-to-be United States—in this interpretation,
the Declaration is a singular instrument born from a response to injustice that was
intended to announce the birth of a new kind of nation and win foreign allies to that
nation's cause. But this interpretation neglects to place the Declaration in the larger
context of eighteenth-century Western political philosophy—the Declaration was only
one of several significant works published during 1776, a remarkable year for political
thought.
Which statement, if true, would most strongly support the claim in the underlined
portion?

Newspapers in 1776 were often read aloud in public places, ensuring that even
those who did not read newspapers themselves could still knowledgeably participate

In late 1776, Benjamin Franklin traveled to France to seek French support for the

George Campbell's The Philosophy of Rhetoric, a highly influential attempt to

In 1776, the English historian Edward Gibbon began publishing The History of the

collapse proved politically influential.

Choice D ("In 1776, the English historian Edward Gibbon began publishing The History of the
Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, a work whose novel theories of empire
collapse proved politically influential.") is correct because it accurately summarizes the structural progression and communicative purpose of the passage.

The 2017 data viewed in time-lapse show greater disparities between polar and

Choice C ("The 2017 data viewed in time-lapse appear to show the oval of elevated

several hours.") is correct because it provides the strongest textual evidence that directly supports or illustrates the claim in the passage.

New Guinea singing dogs, a closely related species, began interbreeding with

Choice A ("The continent-wide population structure of modern dingoes matches that of the
dingoes that were present in Australia around 2,000 years ago.") is correct because it provides the strongest textual evidence that directly supports or illustrates the claim in the passage.

p: Psychologist Lisa K. and colleagues presented participants with several series of images of an everyday object, progressing from blurry to clear, and asked participants to identify the object as soon as they confidently could (on average, at image 12 of 15). Participants were then asked to return to each series and recall at which point they were able to identify the image; on average, they selected image 10. This phenomenon —believing that one knew more in the past than one actually did—is known as hindsight bias. When participants were asked to estimate when a person who had not participated in the experiment would be able to identify the object, the average selection was again image 10. This finding suggests that .

people tend to believe that they are less likely than their peers are to show hindsight

being implicitly reminded of their earlier state of ignorance may enable people to

a form of hindsight bias may occur even when it does not directly enable people to

having their own hindsight bias explicitly pointed out to them may not prevent people

Choice C ("a form of hindsight bias may occur even when it does not directly enable people to
exaggerate their own past knowledge.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

p: The Lex Licinia sumptuaria of 103 BCE was one in a succession of ancient Roman sumptuary laws governing expenditures on luxury, primarily regulating ceremonial processions and other lavish events. Such laws, enacted against a backdrop of anxiety about social dynamism, were intended to limit aspirational overreaching for status but were infrequently enforced. Moreover, enforcement was generally limited to fines, which, when levied against high-profile offenders, were widely announced. The affluent accepted fines as a tax on privilege, even as the amounts increased with frequent revisions to the laws. Historians have therefore argued that enforcing sumptuary laws only minimally may have been a way to avoid undermining the laws' aims, given that .

o:

authorities focused enforcement on the wealthiest offenders, recognizing that
pursuing offenders who were unable to pay the fines could weaken fines'
effectiveness as a deterrent.

less-affluent citizens were reluctant to risk incurring a fine and thus voluntarily
complied with the laws even in the absence of regular enforcement.
e:
Choice A ("the public announcement of fines could signal offenders' wealth and status, placing
enforcement of the laws in conflict with their intent.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

p: In 2014, Marianne Dehasque et al. challenged earlier theories on causes of woolly mammoth extinction that emphasized isolation and inbreeding and a resulting increase in genetic variation and increase in chances of harmful genetic mutations. By pointing out that the flatness of Asimov's characters is a feature of Nemesis and

By agreeing that Asimov's prose is flawed but disagreeing about the quality of his

By asserting that Asimov's minimal characterization is likely a conscious choice that

p: In 1967, archaeologist James Mellaart claimed that at its peak, Çatalhöyük—a 33-acre Neolithic village in present-day Turkey that dates from approximately 7100 to 5950 BCE —housed between 8,000 to 10,000 residents, an estimate based on the excavation of dense clusters of mud brick buildings that were thought to have been dwellings. Arguing that such estimates should be reevaluated, Ian Kuijt and Arkadiusz Marciniak (2024) cite radiocarbon data and ethnographic modeling that suggest the heterogeneity of building use in Çatalhöyük, with many individual buildings being inhabited for relatively brief periods—20 to 30 years or less—before being abandoned or repurposed for nonresidential functions (e.g., storage). Accordingly, these recent findings challenge the assumption that .
q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
o:
the buildings excavated at Çatalhöyük at the time of Mellaart's research had served
a residential purpose as early as 7100 BCE.

the density of excavated buildings at Çatalhöyük can serve as a proxy for how many
people inhabited the village at a given time.

the use of mud bricks is a reliable indicator that a structure had been used either as
a dwelling or for nonresidential purposes.

the number of buildings at Çatalhöyük would have been sufficient to accommodate a
population that expanded from 8,000 to 10,000 inhabitants by 5950 BCE.
e:
Choice B ("the density of excavated buildings at Çatalhöyük can serve as a proxy for how many
people inhabited the village at a given time.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

p:
Though previous studies, including work by Jacobsen et al. (2005), have documented
that wood density correlates negatively with resistance to water stress in angiosperm
taxa, Trueba et al. (2017) observed no such associations among New Caledonian
woody angiosperms. Trueba et al. noted that while several earlier studies included a
variety of habitats—wet and dry forests, savannas—and thus comprised plants with a
wide range of functional trait values, the New Caledonian investigation was restricted to
rainforest taxa occupying climatically similar habitats, resulting in constrained ranges of
such values.
q: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
o:
To indicate that wood density and water-stress resistance correlations in
angiosperms vary significantly depending on the geographic region and climate
conditions studied

To explain the apparent absence of a previously observed association between two
functional traits in angiosperm species sampled from an ecologically homogeneous
set of habitats

To describe a study whose results demonstrate that a known relationship between
two functional traits in angiosperms cannot be observed when sampling is restricted
to homogeneous habitats

To clarify why a geographically restricted study invalidated the finding that
angiosperm species exhibit a trade-off between wood density and water-stress
resistance

Choice B ("To explain the apparent absence of a previously observed association between two
functional traits in angiosperm species sampled from an ecologically homogeneous
set of habitats") is correct because it accurately summarizes the structural progression and communicative purpose of the passage.

p:
Marketing research recognizes three distinct types of price endings: round (like $25.00),
just-below (like $24.99), and precise (like $24.63). A number of studies have
documented significant differences in how frequently these price endings appear in
different countries' marketplaces. Although these variations could be attributable to
cultural factors, researchers have yet to thoroughly investigate that connection, and it
remains unclear which cultural differences may be relevant or how they might interact
with other socioeconomic conditions.
q: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
o: To analyze consumer purchasing behavior across different cultures
To contrast cultural and socioeconomic explanations for differences in price endings

To present the finding that three different pricing strategies are used broadly across
cultures
To identify a research gap regarding potential cultural influences on price endings
e: Choice D ("To identify a research gap regarding potential cultural influences on price endings") is correct because it accurately summarizes the structural progression and communicative purpose of the passage.

p:
A light-year measures distance, not time, despite its potentially misleading name. It
represents the distance that light travels through a vacuum in one Earth year—
approximately 5.88 trillion miles or 9.46 trillion kilometers. Astronomers use this unit
because conventional distance measures are impractical for cosmic scales. For context,
Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to our solar system, is 4.24 light-years away, while
the Andromeda Galaxy lies approximately 2.537 million light-years from Earth.
q: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
o:
It highlights fundamental challenges in measuring vast cosmic distances, identifies
limitations of conventional measurement units, proposes alternative approaches to
conceptualizing space, and suggests how astronomical measurements might be
improved in the future.

It corrects a possible misconception about a scientific term, provides its precise
definition with numerical equivalents, explains why the unit is used in astronomy,
and offers examples of its application to cosmic objects.

It contrasts various astronomical measurement systems, analyzes the advantages
and limitations of each method, evaluates their accuracy for different cosmic scales,
and demonstrates how they complement each other.

It chronicles the historical evolution of astronomical measurement techniques,
describes how earlier distance calculations were performed, explains how the light-
year concept was developed by scientists, and gives two examples of distances
measured in light-years.
e:
Choice B ("It corrects a possible misconception about a scientific term, provides its precise
definition with numerical equivalents, explains why the unit is used in astronomy,
and offers examples of its application to cosmic objects.") is correct because it accurately summarizes the structural progression and communicative purpose of the passage.

p: Humans are overwhelmingly right-hand dominant (85—90%) and can thus be said to exhibit strong population-level right-handedness (PLRH). Among studies of nonhuman primates, William C. McGrew's 1988 study of captive gorillas purported to show PLRH, while William C. McGrew and colleagues' 1999 study of wild chimpanzees did not. Overall, the studies claiming PLRH in nonhuman primates find much lower incidences of right-handedness than humans exhibit, but it's worth noting that studies of captive primates tend to show significantly greater incidences of right-handedness than studies of wild primates do, therefore raising the possibility that .
q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
o:
the apparent discrepancy between the studies' results may be partly attributable to
the 1988 study using different criteria when assessing hand dominance than were
used in the 1999 study.

the greater exposure to humans among the captive gorillas induced them to acquire
more right-handed behaviors.

the number of individuals in the study of wild chimpanzees is insufficient to preclude
the claim that nonhuman primates exhibit PLRH.

the number of individuals in the study of captive gorillas is insufficient for a robust
claim regarding evidence of PLRH.
e:
Choice B ("the greater exposure to humans among the captive gorillas induced them to acquire
more right-handed behaviors.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

p:
In The Jazz Continuum, LaTasha Barnes, Quynn Johnson, and other dancers
seamlessly interweave recent dance styles, including breaking and waacking, with
elements of the Lindy Hop, a popular swing dance of the 1930s with roots in the Black
American community of Harlem, New York. Inspired by Barnes's curiosity about the
similarities between the Lindy Hop and these seemingly unrelated dance styles, the
show's choreography makes visible how intertwined their histories actually are. The
show is therefore a testament to the Lindy Hop's enduring influence on American
culture.
q:
Which choice best states the function of the underlined portion in the text as a
whole?
o:
It addresses the reasons why the historical connections between the dance styles
mentioned earlier in the text have been generally overlooked.

It provides evidence for the text's claim that the Lindy Hop has had a greater cultural
impact than the other dances featured in The Jazz Continuum have had.

It identifies the specific ways in which the Lindy Hop is similar to the contemporary
dance styles discussed in the text.

It identifies the motivation for The Jazz Continuum's choreographic approach that is
described earlier in the text.
e:
Choice D ("It identifies the motivation for The Jazz Continuum's choreographic approach that is
described earlier in the text.") is correct because it accurately summarizes the structural progression and communicative purpose of the passage.

q:
Narratives of American revolutionary history often imply that the US Declaration of
Independence (published in 1776) was a document that specifically resulted from the
presumably exceptional nature of the soon-to-be United States—in this interpretation,
the Declaration is a singular instrument born from a response to injustice that was
intended to announce the birth of a new kind of nation and win foreign allies to that
nation's cause. But this interpretation neglects to place the Declaration in the larger
context of eighteenth-century Western political philosophy—the Declaration was only
one of several significant works published during 1776, a remarkable year for political
thought.
Which statement, if true, would most strongly support the claim in the underlined
portion?
o:
Newspapers in 1776 were often read aloud in public places, ensuring that even
those who did not read newspapers themselves could still knowledgeably participate
in political discussions.

In late 1776, Benjamin Franklin traveled to France to seek French support for the
American cause, eventually leading to France providing both military and financial
aid to the Americans.

George Campbell's The Philosophy of Rhetoric, a highly influential attempt to
develop a foundational theory of how humans communicate, was published in 1776.

In 1776, the English historian Edward Gibbon began publishing The History of the
Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, a work whose novel theories of empire
collapse proved politically influential.
e:
Choice D ("In 1776, the English historian Edward Gibbon began publishing The History of the
Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, a work whose novel theories of empire
collapse proved politically influential.") is correct because it accurately summarizes the structural progression and communicative purpose of the passage.

p:
Text 1
In parts of New Zealand, the stoat is a major predator of the house mouse. Researcher
G.L. Blackwell and colleagues found that when this predation pressure on house mice
was temporarily reduced, their numbers significantly increased. This finding illustrates a
foundational ecological principle: predators control prey population numbers.
Text 2
François Potvin and colleagues found that excluding wolves from a site in Quebec,
Canada, where they typically prey on white-tailed deer had no significant effect on
white-tailed deer abundance. Many other predation-reduction studies show an increase
in prey abundance, but those studies often focus on small, rapidly reproducing prey, like
birds, mice, and frogs, rather than large, slowly reproducing prey, like white-tailed deer,
which could account for the difference between these results and Potvin and
colleagues' results.
q:
Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely agree with which
statement about the "principle" mentioned in Text 1?
o:
It has been challenged by some studies, but the findings of those studies have not
been widely accepted.
It is plausible, but many of the studies that support it have methodological flaws.

It has some evidential support, but it should not be regarded as universally
applicable.

It may be true for some predators but only because those predators share certain
physical characteristics.
e:
Choice C ("It has some evidential support, but it should not be regarded as universally
applicable.") is the correct answer. It best satisfies the prompt requirements based on the textual evidence.

q:
O'Donoghue et al. (2021) analyzed temperature data of Jupiter's upper atmosphere
observed in 2016 and 2017. When superimposed on a map of Jupiter, time-lapse data
representing several hours of observations from one day in 2016 and one day in 2017
indicate an overall temperature gradient from the poles to the equator, with highest
temperatures occurring at the poles, which undergo auroral heating. But the 2017 data
exhibit a large oval of unusually elevated temperature separated from the aurora at one
pole by a band of cooler atmosphere. No other known heating mechanism on Jupiter
could account for the formation of this anomalous structure, so one hypothesis
considered was that it was ejected from the auroral region toward the equator.
Which finding about Jupiter's upper atmosphere, if true, would most strongly
support the hypothesis as described in the text?
o:
Comparing the data observed in 2016 with those observed in 2017 suggests that the
anomalous oval of elevated temperature began forming in 2016.

According to the data, auroral temperatures in 2016 were higher than those in 2017,
although in both years the highest observed temperatures were harbored in auroral
zones.

The 2017 data viewed in time-lapse appear to show the oval of elevated
temperature drifting slightly away from the area of auroral heating over a period of
several hours.

The 2017 data viewed in time-lapse show greater disparities between polar and
equatorial temperatures at the beginning of the observation period than at the end of
the period observed.
e:
Choice C ("The 2017 data viewed in time-lapse appear to show the oval of elevated
temperature drifting slightly away from the area of auroral heating over a period of
several hours.") is correct because it provides the strongest textual evidence that directly supports or illustrates the claim in the passage.

p: The advent of online streaming has led many music listeners to drift away from ownership of music (through downloads or through physical media such as compact discs) and toward the streaming services iHeartRadio and Tidal, among others. Datta et al. studied the impact of this change on the variety of music that listeners consume. listeners who use streaming services would be more likely to give physical copies of

music publishers who choose to forgo releasing music on physical media are likely

the music choices of listeners who use streaming services would likely be more
varied than those of listeners who do not use streaming services.

listeners who prefer to purchase compact discs rather than use a service such as

Choice C ("the music choices of listeners who use streaming services would likely be more
varied than those of listeners who do not use streaming services.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.

p:
Text 1:
For decades, ornithologists assumed that if they saw a singing Bell's vireo—a bird
species found in temperate North America—they must be observing a male trying to
attract a mate or claim territory. As Peter J.B. Slater and Nigel I. Mann have
emphasized, however, a similar assumption can't be made about birds in the tropics,
where females sing as often as males do. Slater and Mann call for more research on
this discrepancy between tropical and temperate female birdsong.
Text 2:
Recent evidence shows that a female Bell's vireo is as capable of song as a male is. In
fact, female birdsong is more common among temperate species than currently
assumed, claim Evangeline Rose and colleagues. These female songbirds sing less
frequently than males do, and in duller tones, making it "easy for researchers to miss
the quiet and hidden females and focus on the loud and colorful males," says Rose.
q:
Based on the texts, how would Rose and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond
to the assertion by Slater and Mann (Text 1) about the different prevalence of
female birdsong in temperate and tropical areas?

They would raise the possibility that the difference in prevalence may be due to
differences in the timing of the mating season among temperate and tropical bird
species.

They would argue that the apparent difference in prevalence may partly reflect a
difference in the ease with which female birdsong and male birdsong can be
detected.

They would caution that the seeming difference in prevalence may be an artifact of
researchers' tendency to study birdsong among temperate species more frequently
than among tropical species.

They would concede that the geographic difference in prevalence is real but argue
that the frequency with which male tropical birds sing has been overstated by
previous researchers.
e:
Choice B ("They would argue that the apparent difference in prevalence may partly reflect a
difference in the ease with which female birdsong and male birdsong can be
detected.") is the correct answer. It best satisfies the prompt requirements based on the textual evidence.

q:

q:
A student is writing an essay about how writers of the late 1700s responded to the
French Revolution and wants to include two pieces of textual evidence that show
closely aligned attitudes toward the revolution. The student has selected the following
quotation, adapted from Helen Maria Williams's 1791 poem "A Farewell, for Two Years,
to England":
In new-born majesty [France] seems to rise,
While sudden from the land oppression flies.
So, at the solemn hour of Nature's birth,
When brooding darkness veil'd the beauteous earth,
Heaven's awful mandate pierc'd the solid night,
"Let there be light," it said, "and there was light!"
Which quotation from another prominent writer of the same period would be most
effective for the student to include along with the quotation from Williams's

"[Liberty] scorns to disdain / Her righteous cause with carnage, and resigns / To

"Reason has, at last, shown her captivating face, beaming with benevolence; and it

Choice D (""Reason has, at last, shown her captivating face, beaming with benevolence; and it

q:

Hummingbirds' preferences are primarily driven by trait-matching between their bills

p:

p: The Lex Licinia sumptuaria of 103 BCE was one in a succession of ancient Roman sumptuary laws governing expenditures on luxury, primarily regulating ceremonial processions and other lavish events. The affluent accepted fines as a tax on privilege, even as the amounts increased with frequent revisions to the laws. Historians have therefore argued that enforcing sumptuary laws only minimally may have been a way to avoid undermining the laws' aims, given that .

the public announcement of fines could signal offenders' wealth and status, placing

the few fines that were imposed under the laws were tolerable to wealthy offenders

less-affluent citizens were reluctant to risk incurring a fine and thus voluntarily

enforcement of the laws in conflict with their intent.") is correct because it presents the most logical conclusion that unifies and completes the train of thought without introducing unwarranted assumptions.
